LESSON: LISTENING AND SPEAKING 5.1.1 PRONUNCIATION: SOUNDS AND WORD STRESS

Grade: SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven
Subject: ENGLISH
Strand: Strand 5
Topic 5.1: Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation: Sounds and Word Stress
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 2

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation: Sounds and Word Stress, part of Strand 5 in SNE  /  physical-impairment / Grade seven ENGLISH.

Key inquiry question: Why is it important to articulate sounds correctly?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

Refer to the KICD curriculum reference at the end of this lesson for the full list of outcomes.

SECTION 3: KEY CONCEPTS AND EXPLANATION

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

Follow your teacher’s guidance for group work, discussion, and practice on this topic.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Listening and Speaking 5.1.1 Pronunciation: Sounds and Word Stress together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
 Digital Literacy is developed as the learner selects digital technology to watch and listen to audio visual recordings on

consonants and vowel sounds

 Communication is developed as learner speaks clearly and effectively while articulating the consonant and vowel sounds

correctly.

 Collaboration is developed as the learner actively participates when making recording of the target vowel and consonant

sounds.

41

Values:
Unity is enhanced as the learner displays team spirit while working with peers to record words with vowel and consonant

sounds.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs)

 Self-esteem is enhanced as the learner practises pronunciation of vowel and consonant sounds.

 Social cohesion is enhanced as the learner makes sentences on family relationships.

Link to other subjects:

The learner relates the concept of correct articulation to their learning in Kiswahili.
